https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ACDCConverter.label: ACDCConverter
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ACDCConverter.comment: A unit with valves for three phases, together with unit control equipment, essential protective and switching devices, DC storage capacitors, phase reactors and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACDCConverterContr.label: ACDCConverterController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACDCConverterContr.comment: ACDC converter unit control. According to IEC 60633, it is the control system used for the controlling, monitoring and protection of a single converter unit.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ACDCTerminal.label: ACDCTerminal
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ACDCTerminal.comment: An electrical connection point (AC or DC) to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACEmulationControl.label: ACEmulationControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACEmulationControl.comment:
The AC emulation control function is used when AC emulation model is activated for a DC system. It consists in computing the active power set point of the DC system as a function of the voltage angle difference between both points of common coupling with the AC network in order to mimic the behavior of an AC transmission line. This control mode enables the automatic adjustment of the active power reference following variations of the AC system operational point. 
The setpoint of the DC system is calculated by Psetpoint=Pref+Kdc*(angle1-angle2), where
- Pref is the existing active power setpoint; 
- Kdc is the control system gain and  
- angle1 and angle2 are the phase angle measurement (measured at points of common coupling with the AC network) respectively at the side 1 and 2 of the DC system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACPointOfCommonCou.label: ACPointOfCommonCoupling
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACPointOfCommonCou.comment: Point of interconnection of the DC converter station to the adjacent AC system (IEC 60633).

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACTieCorridor.label: ACTieCorridor
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ACTieCorridor.comment: A collection of one or more AC tie lines that connect two different control areas.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ActivePower.label: ActivePower
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ActivePower.comment: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ActivePowerChan.label: ActivePowerChangeRate
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ActivePowerChan.comment: Rate of change of active power per time.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ActivePowerControl.label: ActivePowerControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ActivePowerControl.comment: Active power control function is a function block that calculates operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target active power.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AmbientTemperature.label: AmbientTemperatureDependencyCurve
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AmbientTemperature.comment: A curve or functional relationship between the ambient temperature independent variable (X-axis) and relative temperature dependent (Y-axis) variables.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AreaDispatchableUn.label: AreaDispatchableUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AreaDispatchableUn.comment: Allocates a given producing or consuming unit, including direct current corridor and collection of units, to a given control area (through the scheduling area) for supporting the control of the given area through dispatch instruction.

extraRules.name: C:NC:ER:AreaDispatchableUnit:associations
extraRules.description: The AreaDispatchableUnit shall be associated with either GeneratingUnit, PowerElecronicsUnit, EnergyConsumer, ScheduleResource or HydroPump.
extraRules.message: AreaDispatchableUnit is not associated with either GeneratingUnit, PowerElecronicsUnit, EnergyConsumer, ScheduleResource or HydroPump.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AreaInterchangeCon.label: AreaInterchangeController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AreaInterchangeCon.comment: Area interchange control is set to control active power of an area.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AutomationBlockGro.label: AutomationBlockGroup
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AutomationBlockGro.comment: Grouping of function block that are operated with the same priority as settings.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AutomationFunction.label: AutomationFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#AutomationFunction.comment: Automation function is a collection of functional block or other automation function that can be executed as a work cycle program as part of an automated system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BaseOverloadLimitC.label: BaseOverloadLimitCurve
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BaseOverloadLimitC.comment:
A curve or functional relationship between 
- the relative loading - current loading over permanent loading (PATL) independent variable (X-axis), and 
- temporary overloading (TATL) limiting dependent (Y-axis) variables.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BiddingZone.label: BiddingZone
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BiddingZone.comment: A bidding zone is a market-based method for handling power transmission congestion. It consists of scheduling areas that include the relevant production (supply) and consumption (demand) to form an electrical area with the same market price without capacity allocation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BiddingZoneBorder.label: BiddingZoneBorder
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BiddingZoneBorder.comment: A unidirectional interface between two adjacent Bidding Zones, representing the available transmission capacity from the Bidding Zone defined by the association FromBiddingZone (source) to the Bidding Zone defined by the association ToBiddingZone (sink). It defines the capacity constraints and market-based allocation mechanisms for cross-zonal electricity exchange in the specified direction, considering potential transmission congestion and market price differences.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BipolarDCSystem.label: BipolarDCSystem
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#BipolarDCSystem.comment: Bipolar DC system (IEC 60633) consists of two poles of opposite polarity with respect to earth. The overhead lines, if any, of the two poles may be carried on common or separate towers.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Boolean.label: Boolean
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Boolean.comment: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CapacityCalculatio.label: CapacityCalculationRegion
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CapacityCalculatio.comment: Capacity calculation region is a coherent part of the interconnected system that is used for calculating the transmission capacity for a bidding zone or between bidding zones.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Circuit.label: Circuit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Circuit.comment: A circuit is a collection of equipment in a network graph that provide common stability limits. The relevant equipment is in general given by the identifying terminal. A software application that can do topology processing shall calculate the equipment belonging to the circuit, if there are no stability limits associated to it. In case of stability limits, the containment reflects the equipments that were used in the calculation/analysis.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CircuitShare.label: CircuitShare
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CircuitShare.comment: Defines the share of the circuit which is part of an associated power transfer corridor.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ClosedDistribution.label: ClosedDistributionSystemOperator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ClosedDistribution.comment: A system operator which distributes electricity (or gas) within a geographically confined industrial, commercial or shared services and does not supply household customers.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CompensatorControl.label: CompensatorController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CompensatorControl.comment: Compensator controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the use of the compensators.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ConductingEquip.label: ConductingEquipment
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ConductingEquip.comment: The parts of the AC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through terminals.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Conductor.label: Conductor
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Conductor.comment: Combination of conducting material with consistent electrical characteristics, building a single electrical system, used to carry current between points in the power system.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ConnectivityNod.label: ConnectivityNode
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ConnectivityNod.comment: Connectivity nodes are points where terminals of AC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ConnectivityNod.label: ConnectivityNodeContainer
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ConnectivityNod.comment: A base class for all objects that may contain connectivity nodes or topological nodes.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ControlArea.label: ControlArea
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ControlArea.comment:
A control area is a grouping of generating units and/or loads and a cutset of tie lines (as terminals) which may be used for a variety of purposes including automatic generation control, power flow solution area interchange control specification, and input to load forecasting. All generation and load within the area defined by the terminals on the border are considered in the area interchange control. Note that any number of overlapping control area specifications can be superimposed on the physical model. The following general principles apply to ControlArea:
1.  The control area orientation for net interchange is positive for an import, negative for an export.
2.  The control area net interchange is determined by summing flows in Terminals. The Terminals are identified by creating a set of TieFlow objects associated with a ControlArea object. Each TieFlow object identifies one Terminal.
3.  In a single network model, a tie between two control areas must be modelled in both control area specifications, such that the two representations of the tie flow sum to zero.
4.  The normal orientation of Terminal flow is positive for flow into the conducting equipment that owns the Terminal. (i.e. flow from a bus into a device is positive.) However, the orientation of each flow in the control area specification must align with the control area convention, i.e. import is positive. If the orientation of the Terminal flow referenced by a TieFlow is positive into the control area, then this is confirmed by setting TieFlow.positiveFlowIn flag TRUE. If not, the orientation must be reversed by setting the TieFlow.positiveFlowIn flag FALSE.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ControlFunctionBlo.label: ControlFunctionBlock
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ControlFunctionBlo.comment: Control function block is a function block that contains an algorithm for controlling the equipment.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CoordinatedCapacit.label: CoordinatedCapacityCalculator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CoordinatedCapacit.comment: A role that coordinates and executes the task of calculating transmission capacity.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Currency.label: Currency
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Currency.comment: Monetary currencies.  ISO 4217 standard including 3-character currency code.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CurrentControlFunc.label: CurrentControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CurrentControlFunc.comment: Current control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment  to achieve the target current.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopContro.label: CurrentDroopControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopContro.comment: Current droop control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target current.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopOverri.label: CurrentDroopOverride
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#CurrentDroopOverri.comment:
Current droop override uses the following logic:
- When the current exceeds a threshold the device executes the following transitions: 1) When injecting an inductive voltage or in monitoring mode the device tends to inject a voltage proportional to the difference between the line current and the aforementioned threshold. 2) When injecting a capacitive voltage the device transitions to monitoring mode. 
- If the aforementioned proportional voltage is lower than the initial one, the voltage injection remains unchanged. 
Current droop override is not applied when the device operates in currentDroop mode.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#CurrentFlow.label: CurrentFlow
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#CurrentFlow.comment: Electrical current with sign convention: positive flow is out of the conducting equipment into the connectivity node. Can be both AC and DC.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Curve.label: Curve
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Curve.comment: A multi-purpose curve or functional relationship between an independent variable (X-axis) and dependent (Y-axis) variables.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#CurveData.label: CurveData
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#CurveData.comment: Multi-purpose data points for defining a curve.  The use of this generic class is discouraged if a more specific class can be used to specify the X and Y axis values along with their specific data types.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCBiPole.label: DCBiPole
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCBiPole.comment: DC system bipole (IEC 60633), which is part of an DC system consisting of two independently operable DC system poles, which during normal operation, exhibit opposite direct voltage polarities with respect to earth.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCBreaker.label: DCBreaker
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCBreaker.comment: A breaker within a DC system.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCBusbar.label: DCBusbar
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCBusbar.comment: A busbar within a DC system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCBypassSwitch.label: DCBypassSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCBypassSwitch.comment: By-pass switch (IEC 60633) is a high-speed DC switch connected across each converter valve group in DC schemes using more than one independent converter per pole, designed to close rapidly to bypass a converter group that is being taken out of service and commutate the current back into a valve group that is being taken back in service. A by-pass switch may also be used for prolonged shunting of the bridge(s).

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCChopper.label: DCChopper
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCChopper.comment: Low resistance equipment used in the internal DC circuit to balance voltages. It has typically positive and negative pole terminals and a ground.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCCommutationSwitc.label: DCCommutationSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCCommutationSwitc.comment: DC commutation switch (IEC 60633) is a type of high-speed DC switch specifically designed to commutate load current into an alternative parallel current path.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCConductingEqu.label: DCConductingEquipment
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCConductingEqu.comment: The parts of the DC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through DC terminals.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCConverterParalle.label: DCConverterParallelingSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCConverterParalle.comment: Converter paralleling switch (IEC 60633) is a high-speed DC switch connected in series with each converter at the DC terminal in DC schemes where two or more converters are connected in parallel onto a common pole conductor, designed to allow additional converter(s) to be connected in parallel or disconnected without affecting the load current in the other converter.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCConverterUnit.label: DCConverterUnit
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCConverterUnit.comment: Indivisible operative unit comprising all equipment between the point of common coupling on the AC side and the point of common coupling – DC side, essentially one or more converters, together with one or more converter transformers, converter control equipment, essential protective and switching devices and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCCurrentControlFu.label: DCCurrentControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCCurrentControlFu.comment: DC current control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment  to achieve the target current.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCDisconnector.label: DCDisconnector
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCDisconnector.comment: A disconnector within a DC system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCEarthReturnTrans.label: DCEarthReturnTransferSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCEarthReturnTrans.comment: Earth return transfer switch (IEC 60633) DC commutation switch used to transfer DC current from a metallic return path to an earth return path. In some applications, this function is performed by a by-pass switch. Although the term "earth return transfer breaker" has been widely used in the industry for many years, it is misleading since such switches have no ability to interrupt fault current.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCEquipmentCont.label: DCEquipmentContainer
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCEquipmentCont.comment: A modelling construct to provide a root class for containment of DC as well as AC equipment. The class differ from the EquipmentContaner for AC in that it may also contain DCNode-s. Hence it can contain both AC and DC equipment.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCGround.label: DCGround
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCGround.comment: A ground within a DC system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCHarmonicFilter.label: DCHarmonicFilter
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCHarmonicFilter.comment: DC harmonic filter (IEC 60633) is a filter which, in conjunction with the DC reactor(s) and with the DC surge capacitor(s), if any, serves the primary function of reducing (current or voltage) ripple on the DC transmission line and/or earth electrode line.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCHighSpeedSwitch.label: DCHighSpeedSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCHighSpeedSwitch.comment: High-speed DC switch (IEC 60633) is a type of switchgear used on a DC scheme, required to open or close rapidly (< 1 s), including in some cases the need to commutate load current into a parallel conducting path, but with no requirement to interrupt fault or load current. DC switchgear is usually based on a single-phase unit of an AC circuit-breaker, appropriately modified for their DC applications. Their capabilities to perform faster opening and closing than disconnect switches are used but the function of breaking short-circuit currents is not required.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCLine.label: DCLine
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCLine.comment: Overhead lines and/or cables connecting two or more HVDC substations.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCLineParallelingS.label: DCLineParallelingSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCLineParallelingS.comment: Line paralleling switch (IEC 60633) DC commutation switch placed in series with one or more high-voltage pole conductors, allowing two or more lines to be connected in parallel or to revert to single-line operation while conducting load current.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCLineSegment.label: DCLineSegment
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCLineSegment.comment: A wire or combination of wires not insulated from one another, with consistent electrical characteristics, used to carry direct current between points in the DC region of the power system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCMetalicReturnSwi.label: DCMetalicReturnSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCMetalicReturnSwi.comment: Metallic return transfer switch (IEC 60633) is a DC commutation switch used to transfer DC current from an earth return path to a metallic return path. Although the term "metallic return transfer breaker" has been widely used in the industry for many years, it is misleading since such switches have no ability to interrupt fault current.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCNeutralBusGround.label: DCNeutralBusGroundingSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCNeutralBusGround.comment: Neutral bus grounding switch (IEC 60633) or a neutral bus earthing switch is a DC commutation switch connected from the neutral bus to the station earth mat on a bipolar DC scheme, designed to provide a temporary earth connection in the event of an open circuit fault on the electrode line until the imbalance of current between the two poles can be reduced to a safe minimum level or the electrode line connection can be restored.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCNeutralBusSwitch.label: DCNeutralBusSwitch
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCNeutralBusSwitch.comment: Neutral bus switch (IEC 60633) is a DC commutation switch connected in series with the neutral bus on a bipolar DC scheme, designed to commutate current out of the pole conductor or neutral bus and into the electrode line or dedicated metallic return conductor or earth in response to a fault in a converter or neutral bus.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCNode.label: DCNode
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCNode.comment: DC nodes are points where terminals of DC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCPointOfCommonCou.label: DCPointOfCommonCoupling
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCPointOfCommonCou.comment: Point of interconnection of the DC converter station to the DC transmission line (IEC 60633).

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCPole.label: DCPole
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCPole.comment: The direct current (DC) system pole (IEC 60633) is part of a DC system consisting of all the equipment in the DC substations and the interconnecting transmission lines, if any, which during normal operation exhibit a common direct voltage polarity with respect to earth.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCSeriesDevice.label: DCSeriesDevice
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCSeriesDevice.comment: A series device within the DC system, typically a reactor used for filtering or smoothing.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCShunt.label: DCShunt
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCShunt.comment: A shunt device within the DC system, typically used for filtering.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSmoothingReactor.label: DCSmoothingReactor
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSmoothingReactor.comment: Reactor (IEC 60633) connected in series with a converter unit or converter units on the DC side for the primary purpose of smoothing the direct current and reducing current transients.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSmoothingReactor.label: DCSmoothingReactorArrester
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSmoothingReactor.comment: Arrester (IEC 60633) connected between the terminals of a smoothing reactor.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSubstation.label: DCSubstation
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSubstation.comment: DC substation or DC converter station (IEC 60633) is part of an DC system which consists of one or more converter units installed in a single location together with buildings, reactors, filters, reactive power supply, control, monitoring, protective, measuring and auxiliary equipment. A DC substation forming part of an DC transmission system may be referred to as an DC transmission substation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSubstationBipole.label: DCSubstationBipole
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSubstationBipole.comment: Part of a bipolar DC system (IEC 60633) contained within a DC substation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSubstationPole.label: DCSubstationPole
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSubstationPole.comment: Part of an DC system pole (IEC 60633) which is contained within a DC substation.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCSwitch.label: DCSwitch
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DCSwitch.comment: A switch within the DC system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSystem.label: DCSystem
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSystem.comment: Electrical power system which transfers energy in the form of direct current between two or more AC buses (defined in IEC 60633).

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSystemDirectionK.label: DCSystemDirectionKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCSystemDirectionK.comment: Direction kinds of the DC system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCTieCorridor.label: DCTieCorridor
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCTieCorridor.comment: A collection of one or more direct current poles that connect two different control areas.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCVoltageControlFu.label: DCVoltageControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DCVoltageControlFu.comment: DC voltage control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target voltage.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Date.label: Date
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Date.comment: Date as "yyyy-mm-dd", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-dd(+/-)hh:mm".

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DateTime.label: DateTime
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#DateTime.comment: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Decimal.label: Decimal
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Decimal.comment: Decimal is the base-10 notational system for representing real numbers.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentBipol.label: DirectCurrentBipoleController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentBipol.comment: DC system bipole control that is the control system of a bipole in accordance with IEC 60633.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentCircu.label: DirectCurrentCircuit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentCircu.comment: A direct current circuit is a circuit consists of direct current equipment.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentEquip.label: DirectCurrentEquipmentController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentEquip.comment: Direct current equipment controller used to control different parts of the hierarchical structure of the DC control system defined by IEC 60633.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentMaste.label: DirectCurrentMasterController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentMaste.comment:
Direct current system control is a control system which governs the operation of an entire DC system consisting of more than one DC substation and performs those functions of controlling, monitoring and protection which require information from more than one substation. This can also be a multiterminal control which is a DC system control for more that two DC substations or a DC master control, which is a general concept for control coordination of a DC system. The DC master control may be implemented at the bipole and/or pole level as defined in IEC 60633. 
The DC system control/multiterminal control/master control is part of the hierarchical structure of an HVDC control system that has an integrated AC/DC system control as the highest level of control which governs the integrated operation of AC and DC systems of a power system. This control system is under the responsibility of the system operator.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentPoleC.label: DirectCurrentPoleController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentPoleC.comment: DC system pole control, which is the control system of a pole in accordance with IEC 60633.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSubst.label: DirectCurrentSubstationBipoleController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSubst.comment: Control system of a substation bipole (IEC 60633).

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSubst.label: DirectCurrentSubstationController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSubst.comment: Control system used for the controlling, monitoring and protection within a DC substation (IEC 60633). A DC substation control may be implemented at the bipole and/or pole level and may be referred to as local control.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSubst.label: DirectCurrentSubstationPoleController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSubst.comment: Control system of a substation pole (IEC 60633).

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSyste.label: DirectCurrentSystemOperator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DirectCurrentSyste.comment: System operator of the direct current pole. There are typically one or two system operators that are operating either the control area at one side or the control areas at both sides of the direct current pole. In some cases it is operated by an operator from the connected control areas.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DistributionSystem.label: DistributionSystemOperator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DistributionSystem.comment: A system operator that is responsible for operating of energy distribution network from transmission level down to low voltage levels including the connection to household.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Duration.label: Duration
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Duration.comment: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DurationOverloadLi.label: DurationOverloadLimitCurve
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#DurationOverloadLi.comment:
A curve or functional relationship between
- the overload duration independent variable (X-axis), and 
- temporary overloading (TATL) limiting dependent (Y-axis) variables.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EdgeControlArea.label: EdgeControlArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EdgeControlArea.comment: An EdgeControlArea representing the local, site-level (edge) operational domain that coordinates one or more Installations and their connections. It is typically operated by an edge operator (e.g., a person/company operating a campus, mall, microgrid, or prosumer cluster) and supports local monitoring, control, scheduling, and limits—both islanded and grid-connected.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EdgeSchedulingArea.label: EdgeSchedulingArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EdgeSchedulingArea.comment:
An EdgeSchedulingArea is a electrical area that is part of a SubSchedulingArea with one or more Installations connected.
It serves as the smallest energy level scheduling, forecasting and aggregated measurement used for coordinating energy production, consumption, and storage across its constituent connections.
An EdgeSchedulingArea may represent physical locations with multiple grid connection, such as a shopping mall, university campus, industrial facility, or private microgrid that are normally connected to the grid.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ElectricalCharging.label: ElectricalChargingUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ElectricalCharging.comment: A unit that supplies electrical power for charging electrical non-stationary entities, e.g. electrical vehicle, trucks, buses, ferries, boats and airplanes. The characteristic is that the energy consumption is highly schedule dependent.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyAlignmentCoo.label: EnergyAlignmentCoordinator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyAlignmentCoo.comment: A role that is responsible for alignment of forecast and schedule energy to a given energy coordination region.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockCompone.label: EnergyBlockComponent
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockCompone.comment: Energy block component where the energy group is distributed according to the energy block order of each energy component in an energy group.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockOrder.label: EnergyBlockOrder
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyBlockOrder.comment: The energy block order is a block (an amount) of energy that forms the sequence of orders that are going to be distributed to an energy block component.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyComponent.label: EnergyComponent
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyComponent.comment: The energy component for a producer or a consumer that has the same energy characteristic, e.g. fuel type and technology.

extraRules.name: C:NC:ER:EnergyComponent:associations
extraRules.description: The EnergyComponent shall be associated with either GeneratingUnit, PowerElecronicsUnit, EnergyConsumer or HydroPump.
extraRules.message: EnergyComponent is not associated with either GeneratingUnit, PowerElecronicsUnit, EnergyConsumer or HydroPump.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EnergyConnectio.label: EnergyConnection
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EnergyConnectio.comment: A connection of energy generation or consumption on the power system model.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EnergyConsumer.label: EnergyConsumer
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EnergyConsumer.comment:
Generic user of energy - a  point of consumption on the power system model.
EnergyConsumer.pfixed, .qfixed, .pfixedPct and .qfixedPct have meaning only if there is no LoadResponseCharacteristic associated with EnergyConsumer or if LoadResponseCharacteristic.exponentModel is set to False.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyCoordination.label: EnergyCoordinationRegion
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyCoordination.comment: A region that has a common organisation or a service that is responsible for alignment of forecast and scheduling of energy.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyExchangePoin.label: EnergyExchangePoint
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyExchangePoin.comment:
An EnergyExchangePoint is a PointOfCommonCoupling that defines the electrical and operational interface between two independent adjacent grid operators —such as two TSOs, a TSO and a DSO, or two DSOs—who are responsible for coordinated operation of interconnected power systems.
It marks the electrical boundary point at which the energy exchange agreement between the two grid operators is enacted, and where power flows, balancing responsibilities, and observability requirements are formally managed. Operational conditions defined by applicable regulation—such as exchange capacity, frequency and voltage support, fault ride-through, protection coordination, and metering—can be defined at this point and in some cases enforced at this point.
It supports bidirectional power flow and may be associated with operational requirements such as balancing, frequency and voltage control, telemetry, protection coordination, and energy accounting.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyGroup.label: EnergyGroup
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyGroup.comment: An energy group is an aggregation of energy components which have the same energy characteristic, e.g. fuel type and technology. It can be used to allocate energy.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyKind.label: EnergyKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyKind.comment: Categories of energy used for energy groups.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergySourceRefere.label: EnergySourceReference
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergySourceRefere.comment: An energy source reference refers to a set of  fuel types characteristic for reporting, e.g. European Energy Certificate System (EECS). The kind of energy should be possible to be linked with different type of energy forecast, e.g. wind production for a given area based on wind forecast.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyType.label: EnergyType
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EnergyType.comment:
A source of the energy.

An energy type reference refers to an energy characteristic that is needed for reporting, e.g. European Energy Certificate System (EECS). The kind of energy should be possible to be linked with different type of energy forecast, e.g. wind production for a given area based on wind forecast.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Equipment.label: Equipment
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Equipment.comment: The parts of a power system that are physical devices, electronic or mechanical.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EquipmentContai.label: EquipmentContainer
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EquipmentContai.comment: A modelling construct to provide a root class for containing equipment.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquipmentControlle.label: EquipmentController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquipmentControlle.comment: Equipment controller is an automation function that can control one or multiple equipment function to achieve all the targets inside the given tolerance.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquivalentGenerati.label: EquivalentGeneratingUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquivalentGenerati.comment: An indivisible set of installations which can generate electrical energy such that the frequency of the generated voltage, the generator speed and the frequency of network voltage are in a constant ratio and thus in synchronism. This is often referred as synchronous power-generating module.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EquivalentInjec.label: EquivalentInjection
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#EquivalentInjec.comment: This class represents equivalent injections (generation or load).  Voltage regulation is allowed only at the point of connection.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquivalentPowerEle.label: EquivalentPowerElectronicsUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquivalentPowerEle.comment: An equivalent unit or ensemble of units generating electricity, which is either non-synchronously connected to the network or connected through power electronics, and that also has a single connection point to a transmission system, distribution system including closed distribution system or an equivalent representation of a HVDC system. This is often referred as power park module.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquivalentPowerPla.label: EquivalentPowerPlant
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#EquivalentPowerPla.comment: Collection of equivalent equipment for purposes of generation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ExceptionalPowerTr.label: ExceptionalPowerTransferCorridor
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ExceptionalPowerTr.comment: Potential power transfer corridor that can be triggered by equipment which changes its in service status or it is operating in an island.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ExternalNetwork.label: ExternalNetworkInjection
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ExternalNetwork.comment: This class represents the external network and it is used for IEC 60909 calculations.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FACTSEquipment.label: FACTSEquipment
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FACTSEquipment.comment: Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System regulating equipment.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FlexibleEnergyUnit.label: FlexibleEnergyUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FlexibleEnergyUnit.comment: Flexible consumer or embedded producer of energy. The unit cannot be a net producer.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Float.label: Float
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Float.comment: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#FossilFuel.label: FossilFuel
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#FossilFuel.comment: The fossil fuel consumed by the non-nuclear thermal generating unit.   For example, coal, oil, gas, etc.   These are the specific fuels that the generating unit can consume.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FrequencyControlFu.label: FrequencyControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FrequencyControlFu.comment: Frequency control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target frequency.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FrequencyMonitorin.label: FrequencyMonitoringTerminal
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FrequencyMonitorin.comment: Frequency monitoring terminal provides location in the model where the frequency is monitored for the purpose of power frequency control.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FuelStorage.label: FuelStorage
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FuelStorage.comment: Fuel storage. e.g. pile of coal that can be shared between multiple thermal generating units.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FunctionBlock.label: FunctionBlock
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FunctionBlock.comment: Function block is a function described as a set of elementary blocks. The blocks describe the function between input variables and output variables.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FunctionInputVaria.label: FunctionInputVariable
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FunctionInputVaria.comment: Functional input variable defines the domain of the function.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FunctionOutputVari.label: FunctionOutputVariable
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#FunctionOutputVari.comment: Functional output variable defines the codomain of the function.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#GateInputPin.label: GateInputPin
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#GateInputPin.comment: Input pin for a logical gate. The condition described in the input pin gives a logical true or false. The result from measurement and calculation are converted to a true or false.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#GeneratingUnit.label: GeneratingUnit
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#GeneratingUnit.comment: A single or set of synchronous machines for converting mechanical power into alternating-current power. For example, individual machines within a set may be defined for scheduling purposes while a single control signal is derived for the set. In this case there would be a GeneratingUnit for each member of the set and an additional GeneratingUnit corresponding to the set.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#GeothermalGenerati.label: GeothermalGeneratingUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#GeothermalGenerati.comment: Generating unit that is generating electrical power from geothermal energy.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#GridConnectionPoin.label: GridConnectionPoint
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#GridConnectionPoin.comment:
A GridConnectionPoint is a Point of Common Coupling (PCC) that defines the contractual and operational interface between a grid operator (e.g., TSO, DSO, or CDSO) and a connecting entity, such as a person, company, prosumer, or facility operator.
It represents the electrical location at which the connection agreement—as defined by applicable grid connection codes (e.g., EU RfG, DCC, HVDC)—is enacted, establishing the technical, legal, and compliance boundaries for power exchange between the public grid and the connected installation or energy system.
All operational conditions required by regulation—such as voltage and frequency ranges, fault ride-through capabilities, power quality limits, and observability—are applicable at this point.
The GridConnectionPoint may support bidirectional power flow, and is typically associated with metering, disconnection, and protection devices, but is independent of voltage level or specific technology.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#HydroPowerPlant.label: HydroPowerPlant
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#HydroPowerPlant.comment: A hydro power station which can generate or pump. When generating, the generator turbines receive water from an upper reservoir. When pumping, the pumps receive their water from a lower reservoir.

extraRules.name: C:NC:ER:HydroPowerPlant:operatingMode
extraRules.description: The SynchronousMachine.operatingMode of all SynchronousMachine objects part of a HydroPowerPlant shall be consistent.
extraRules.message: The SynchronousMachine.operatingMode is not consistent for all SynchronousMachine objects part of a HydroPowerPlant.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#HydroPump.label: HydroPump
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#HydroPump.comment: A synchronous motor-driven pump, typically associated with a pumped storage plant.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns/prof-cim#IRI.label: IRI
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns/prof-cim#IRI.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as rdf:resource in RDFXML.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#IdentifiedObjec.label: IdentifiedObject
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#IdentifiedObjec.comment: This is a root class to provide common identification for all classes needing identification and naming attributes.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ImpedanceControlFu.label: ImpedanceControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ImpedanceControlFu.comment: Impedance control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target impedance.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#InfeedLimit.label: InfeedLimit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#InfeedLimit.comment: Infeed limit set constraints fed in to the network by two or more terminals.

extraRules.name: C:NC:ER:InfeedLimit:requiredAttributes
extraRules.description: An InfeedLimit shall have either .normalValueA or .normalValueW.
extraRules.message: InfeedLimit does not have either .normalValueA or .normalValueW.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#InfeedTerminal.label: InfeedTerminal
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#InfeedTerminal.comment: Infeed terminal defines the terminals that are linked to an infeed limit.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#InjectionControlle.label: InjectionController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#InjectionControlle.comment: Injection controller is controlling the equipment which represents an injection or an external network.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Installation.label: Installation
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Installation.comment:
An Installation represents a functionally integrated system at a premises or facility that is connected to an energy infrastructure, but is not itself an energy device (e.g., generator, load, or storage).
It serves as a system-level abstraction of the internal infrastructure—such as intake cable, switchboards, internal cabling, distribution panels, protection devices, and auxiliary equipment —that enables and constraints the connection to one or more energy connections (electrical, thermal, gas, etc.).

Installations are typically owned and operated by the site holder, not the utility, and exist within buildings, industrial sites, or campus.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Integer.label: Integer
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Integer.comment: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LimitDependencyCur.label: LimitDependencyCurve
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LimitDependencyCur.comment: A curve or functional relationship between an independent variable (X-axis) and limiting dependent (Y-axis) variables.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Line.label: Line
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Line.comment: Contains equipment beyond a substation belonging to a power transmission line.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LineCircuit.label: LineCircuit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LineCircuit.comment: A line circuit is a circuit that has at least one ACLineSegment and may or may not include related switching and/or auxiliary equipment.

extraRules.name: C:NC:ER:Circuit:associations
extraRules.description: The Circuit shall be associated with either Equipment or Terminal.
extraRules.message: Circuit is not associated with either Equipment or Terminal.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyContr.label: LoadFrequencyControlArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyContr.comment: A part of a synchronous area or an entire synchronous area, physically demarcated by points of measurement at interconnectors to other load frequency control (LFC) areas, operated by one or more TSOs fulfilling the obligations of load-frequency control.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyContr.label: LoadFrequencyControlBlock
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyContr.comment: A part of a synchronous area or an entire synchronous area, physically demarcated by points of measurement at interconnectors to other load frequency control (LFC) blocks, consisting of one or more LFC areas, operated by one or more TSOs fulfilling the obligations of load-frequency control.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyContr.label: LoadFrequencyControlOperator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LoadFrequencyContr.comment: A role that is responsible for operational security by operating the load frequency control (LFC) mechanism.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LogicalOperatorsKi.label: LogicalOperatorsKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LogicalOperatorsKi.comment: Kinds of logical operators for comparison.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LossCurve.label: LossCurve
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#LossCurve.comment: Represents the losses in the equipment due to operation position.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#MobileElectricalUn.label: MobileElectricalUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#MobileElectricalUn.comment:
A MobileElectricalUnit represents a persistent power system resource that can act as a source or sink of electrical energy within the grid. It is designed to interface with the grid through defined connection points for charging or discharging, while the physical energy storage asset associated with it (e.g., an electric vehicle or battery trailer) may be mobile. The MobileElectricalUnit abstracts the system-side functionality of mobile energy storage, independent of specific assets or charging events. It typically stores electrical energy in batteries or equivalent storage media and supports flexible, temporary, or location-variable integration into the power system. Examples include, but are not limited to:
  • Electric vehicles (EVs)
  • Electrically powered ferries
  • Trailer-based battery storage units
  • Mobile battery systems for backup or temporary grid support
  • This concept supports consistent modeling of mobile energy systems in grid studies by treating the grid-facing connection as a stable power system element, while the associated physical unit is managed as an asset.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ModularStaticSynch.label: ModularStaticSynchronousSeriesCompensator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ModularStaticSynch.comment: Modular static synchronous series compensator (MSSSC) is a type of flexible AC transmission system regulating equipment which consists of solid-state voltage source inverter connected in series with a transmission line. This is similar to static synchronous series compensator (SSSC), but without injection transformer. This enables the MSSSC to be truly modular with the ability to simply install a number of equipment in series to provide a desired maximum level of impedance. MSSSC can be dispersed into multiple location in a circuit working collectively under the same controller scheme.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#MonitoringArea.label: MonitoringArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#MonitoringArea.comment: A coherent part of the interconnected electrical power system, that includes the system operators' responsibility area and the surrounding parts of other system operators' responsibility area, that need to be monitored for security assessment.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#MonopolarDCSystem.label: MonopolarDCSystem
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#MonopolarDCSystem.comment: Monopolar DC system (IEC 60633) is a DC system with only one pole.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.label: OperationalLimit
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.comment:
A value and normal value associated with a specific kind of limit. 
The sub class value and normalValue attributes vary inversely to the associated OperationalLimitType.acceptableDuration (acceptableDuration for short).  
If a particular piece of equipment has multiple operational limits of the same kind (apparent power, current, etc.), the limit with the greatest acceptableDuration shall have the smallest limit value and the limit with the smallest acceptableDuration shall have the largest limit value.  Note: A large current can only be allowed to flow through a piece of equipment for a short duration without causing damage, but a lesser current can be allowed to flow for a longer duration.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.label: OperationalLimitDirectionKind
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.comment: The direction attribute describes the side of  a limit that is a violation.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.label: OperationalLimitSet
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.comment: A set of limits associated with equipment.  Sets of limits might apply to a specific temperature, or season for example. A set of limits may contain different severities of limit levels that would apply to the same equipment. The set may contain limits of different types such as apparent power and current limits or high and low voltage limits  that are logically applied together as a set.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.label: OperationalLimitType
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OperationalLimi.comment: The operational meaning of a category of limits.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OrdinaryPowerTrans.label: OrdinaryPowerTransferCorridor
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OrdinaryPowerTrans.comment: Power transfer corridor defined for normal operating network.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Organisation.label: Organisation
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Organisation.comment: Organisation that might have roles as utility, contractor, supplier, manufacturer, customer, etc.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OrganisationRol.label: OrganisationRole
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#OrganisationRol.comment: Identifies a way in which an organisation may participate in the utility enterprise (e.g., customer, manufacturer, etc).

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordination.label: OutageCoordinationRegion
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordination.comment: A region that has a common organisation or service responsible for outage planning and coordination and its impact on grid operation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordinator.label: OutageCoordinator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OutageCoordinator.comment: A role that coordinates the planned availability status of relevant power system equipment to meet the need by the asset owner or operator and the security of the power system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OutagePlanningAgen.label: OutagePlanningAgent
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OutagePlanningAgen.comment: An entity with the task of planning the availability status of a relevant power generating module, a relevant demand facility or a relevant grid element.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OverlappingZone.label: OverlappingZone
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#OverlappingZone.comment: A collection of all the overlapping cross border assessed elements which have the same sets of impacted and impacting regions.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PTCTriggeredEquipm.label: PTCTriggeredEquipment
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PTCTriggeredEquipm.comment: Power Transfer Corridor triggered equipment connects the equipment that will create the exceptional power transfer corridor when taking out of service. e.g. A system with three lines gets an exceptional power transfer corridor when one of the lines is taken out of service.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PU.label: PU
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PU.comment: Per Unit - a positive or negative value referred to a defined base. Values typically range from -10 to +10.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PerCent.label: PerCent
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PerCent.comment: Percentage on a defined base.   For example, specify as 100 to indicate at the defined base.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PhaseControlFuncti.label: PhaseControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PhaseControlFuncti.comment: Phase control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target voltage.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminal.label: PinTerminal
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminal.comment: Input pin associated with a Terminal. It is used for comparison.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminalKind.label: PinTerminalKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PinTerminalKind.comment: The kind of quantities that can serve as an input value for the pin.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Plant.label: Plant
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Plant.comment: A Plant is a collection of equipment for purposes of generation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PointOfCommonCoupl.label: PointOfCommonCoupling
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PointOfCommonCoupl.comment: Point of Common Coupling (PCC) refers to the location where multiple electrical sources or loads are electrically connected and provide a reference point where the voltages and currents from different parts of the system are considered to be common. The PCC is used to support system analysis, control, and monitoring, as it provides a reference for understanding the interactions and power flow between various components within the system. It is also relevant to define the requirement and responsibility between different actors in operating a power system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerBlockKind.label: PowerBlockKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerBlockKind.comment: Power block kind describes the increase and/or decrease of power.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerCapacity.label: PowerCapacity
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerCapacity.comment: Power capacity defines the capacity in regard to generation, consumption and transmission (import and export) for a relevant power system resource, e.g. bidding zone, including maximum and minimum electrical power capacity and any capacity allocation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalChe.label: PowerElectricalChemicalUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalChe.comment: A unit capable of either generating electrical energy from chemical reactions or using electrical energy to cause chemical reactions.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalChe.label: PowerElectricalChemicalUnitKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectricalChe.comment: Kind of power electrical chemical unit.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsCo.label: PowerElectronicsConnectionController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsCo.comment: Power electronics connection controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the power electronics connection.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsMa.label: PowerElectronicsMarineUnit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsMa.comment: A unit that capture energy from marine sources, e.g. waves, for generating electrical power.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PowerElectronic.label: PowerElectronicsUnit
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PowerElectronic.comment: A generating unit or battery or aggregation that connects to the AC network using power electronics rather than rotating machines.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsUn.label: PowerElectronicsUnitController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerElectronicsUn.comment: Power electronics unit controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the power electronics unit.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerFactorControl.label: PowerFactorControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerFactorControl.comment: Power factor control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target power factor.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerFrequencyCont.label: PowerFrequencyControlKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerFrequencyCont.comment: Kinds of power frequency control modes.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerFrequencyCont.label: PowerFrequencyController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerFrequencyCont.comment: Power frequency controller is controlling the active power balance as typically done by the secondary control. If an unbalance between the scheduled active power values of each generation unit and the loads plus losses occurs, primary control will adapt (increase/decrease) the active power production of each unit (depending on the power shift key strategy), leading to an over- or under-frequency situation. The secondary frequency controller will then control the frequency back to its nominal value, re- establishing a cost-efficient generation delivered by each unit.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerPlantControll.label: PowerPlantController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerPlantControll.comment: Power plant controller is controlling the equipment of a power plant.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerShiftKeyKind.label: PowerShiftKeyKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerShiftKeyKind.comment: Kind of generating and load shift keys strategy.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerShiftKeyStrat.label: PowerShiftKeyStrategy
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerShiftKeyStrat.comment: Strategy of the power shift key.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerSystemOrganis.label: PowerSystemOrganisationRole
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerSystemOrganis.comment: A role that is responsible for the functional operational of a power system resource.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PowerSystemReso.label: PowerSystemResource
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#PowerSystemReso.comment: A power system resource (PSR) can be an item of equipment such as a switch, an equipment container containing many individual items of equipment such as a substation, or an organisational entity such as sub-control area. Power system resources can have measurements associated.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransferCorri.label: PowerTransferCorridor
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransferCorri.comment: A power transfer corridor is defined as a set of circuits (transmission lines or transformers) separating two portions of the power system, or a subset of circuits exposed to a substantial portion of the transmission exchange between two parts of the system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransformerCi.label: PowerTransformerCircuit
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PowerTransformerCi.comment: A power transformer circuit is a circuit that has at least one PowerTransformer and may or may not include related switching and/or auxiliary equipment.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PropertyReference.label: PropertyReference
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#PropertyReference.comment: The reference to a class and one of its properties.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ProportionalEnergy.label: ProportionalEnergyComponent
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ProportionalEnergy.comment: Serves for grouping components within an energy group, with proportional energy allocation to all components.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Reactance.label: Reactance
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Reactance.comment: Reactance (imaginary part of impedance), at rated frequency.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ReactiveCapabil.label: ReactiveCapabilityCurve
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ReactiveCapabil.comment: Reactive power rating envelope versus the synchronous machine's active power, in both the generating and motoring modes. For each active power value there is a corresponding high and low reactive power limit  value. Typically there will be a separate curve for each coolant condition, such as hydrogen pressure.  The Y1 axis values represent reactive minimum and the Y2 axis values represent reactive maximum.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ReactivePower.label: ReactivePower
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#ReactivePower.comment: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the quadrature component of the current.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ReactivePowerContr.label: ReactivePowerControlFunction
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ReactivePowerContr.comment: Reactive power control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target reactive power.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#RecoveryOverloadLi.label: RecoveryOverloadLimitCurve
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#RecoveryOverloadLi.comment: The relation between the recovery time and an overload limit.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Region.label: Region
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#Region.comment: A region where the system operator belongs to.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#RegulatingCondE.label: RegulatingCondEq
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#RegulatingCondE.comment: A type of conducting equipment that can regulate a quantity (i.e. voltage or flow) at a specific point in the network.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Reservoir.label: Reservoir
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Reservoir.comment: A water storage facility within a hydro system, including: ponds, lakes, lagoons, and rivers. The storage is usually behind some type of dam.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#RotatingMachineCon.label: RotatingMachineController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#RotatingMachineCon.comment: Rotating machine controller is controlling the equipment which may be used as a generator or motor.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SSSCController.label: SSSCController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SSSCController.comment: The controller of a Static synchronous series compensator (SSSC).

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SSSCSimulationSett.label: SSSCSimulationSettings
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SSSCSimulationSett.comment: SSSC control simulation settings used by the algorithm for power flow calculations.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ScheduleResource.label: ScheduleResource
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ScheduleResource.comment: A schedule resource is a market-based method for handling participation of small units, particularly located on the lower voltage level that is controlled by a Distributed System Operator (DSO). It is a collection of units that can operate in the market by providing bids, offers and a resulting committed operational schedule for the collection.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ScheduleResourceCo.label: ScheduleResourceController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ScheduleResourceCo.comment: Schedule resource controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the schedule resource.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SchedulingArea.label: SchedulingArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SchedulingArea.comment: An area where production and/or consumption of energy can be forecasted, scheduled and measured. The area is operated by only one system operator, typically a Transmission System Operator (TSO). The area can consist of a sub area, which has the same definition as the main area, but it can be operated by another system operator (typically Distributed System Operator (DSO) or a Closed Distributed System Operator (CDSO)). This includes microgrid concept. A substation is the smallest grouping that can be included in the area. The area size should be considered in terms of the possibility of accumulated reading (settlement metering) and the capability of operating as an island.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SchedulingAreaExch.label: SchedulingAreaExchangePoint
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SchedulingAreaExch.comment: Combination of scheduling area and one or more energy exchange point to define the relevant exchange point for a given scheduling area.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SecondarySubstatio.label: SecondarySubstation
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SecondarySubstatio.comment:
A SecondarySubstation is a substation that is either supplied by or serves a primary substation. It is responsible for transforming, distributing, or aggregating power to and from installations such as homes, industrial facilities, or prosumer sites.
A secondary substation supports bidirectional power flows, enabling both consumption and injection of energy within the distribution network.
It typically includes transformers, switchgear, protection, and measurement equipment, and may be equipped for remote monitoring or autonomous control

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SecurityCoordinato.label: SecurityCoordinator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SecurityCoordinato.comment: A role that coordinates the relevant remedial actions and their optimisation to ensure efficient use to achieve required operational security of the power system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ShiftMethodKind.label: ShiftMethodKind
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ShiftMethodKind.comment: Kind of shift method. Describes the way a power schedule should be distributed amongst production and consumption. e.g. Type of generating and load shift key.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SolarRadiationDepe.label: SolarRadiationDependencyCurve
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SolarRadiationDepe.comment:
A curve or functional relationship between 
- the solar radiation independent variable (X-axis), and 
- relative dependent (Y-axis) variables.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronousC.label: StaticSynchronousCompensator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronousC.comment: Static synchronous compensator (STATCOM), also known as a static synchronous condenser (STATCON), is a type of flexible AC transmission system regulating equipment used on alternating current electricity transmission networks. It is based on a power electronics voltage-source converter and can act as either a source or sink of reactive AC power to an electricity network. If connected to a source of power it can also provide active AC power.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronousS.label: StaticSynchronousSeriesCompensator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#StaticSynchronousS.comment: Static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) is a type of flexible AC transmission system which consists of a solid-state voltage source inverter coupled with a transformer that is connected in series with a transmission line. This device can inject an almost sinusoidal voltage in series with the line. This injected voltage could be considered as an inductive or capacitive reactance, which is connected in series with the transmission line. This feature can provide controllable voltage compensation. In addition, SSSC is able to reverse the power flow by injecting a sufficiently large series reactive compensating voltage. Moreover it can inject a voltage proportional to the difference between the line current and the pre-configured current threshold.<font color="#636671"> </font>It shall have two Terminal-s associated with it.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#StaticVarCompensat.label: StaticVarCompensator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#StaticVarCompensat.comment:
A facility for providing variable and controllable shunt reactive power. The SVC typically consists of a stepdown transformer, filter, thyristor-controlled reactor, and thyristor-switched capacitor arms.

The SVC may operate in fixed MVar output mode or in voltage control mode. When in voltage control mode, the output of the SVC will be proportional to the deviation of voltage at the controlled bus from the voltage setpoint.  The SVC characteristic slope defines the proportion.  If the voltage at the controlled bus is equal to the voltage setpoint, the SVC MVar output is zero.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#String.label: String
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#String.comment: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns/prof-cim#String.label: StringFixedLanguage
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns/prof-cim#String.comment:
A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.
The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns/prof-cim#String.label: StringIRI
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns/prof-cim#String.comment:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SubControlArea.label: SubControlArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SubControlArea.comment: A SubControlArea representing the operational control domain within a higher-level control area. It is typically operated by a Distribution System Operator (DSO) and covers the monitoring, control, scheduling, and application of operational limits for distribution system resources and exchanges at its boundary.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SubSchedulingArea.label: SubSchedulingArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SubSchedulingArea.comment: An area that is a part of another scheduling area. Typically part of a Transmission System Operator (TSO) scheduling area operated by a Distributed System Operator (DSO) or a Close Distributed System Operator (CDSO). This includes microgrid concept. A sub scheduling area can contain other sub areas. A sub scheduling area leaf will form the smallest entity of any given energy area.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Substation.label: Substation
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#Substation.comment: A collection of equipment for purposes other than generation or utilization, through which electric energy in bulk is passed for the purposes of switching or modifying its characteristics.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SubstationControll.label: SubstationController
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SubstationControll.comment: Substation controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the use of the controlling equipment within a substation.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SynchronousArea.label: SynchronousArea
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SynchronousArea.comment: A synchronous area is an electrical area covered by interconnect with a common system frequency in a steady-state.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#SynchronousMach.label: SynchronousMachine
https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#SynchronousMach.comment: An electromechanical device that operates with shaft rotating synchronously with the network. It is a single machine operating either as a generator or synchronous condenser or pump.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SystemControl.label: SystemControl
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SystemControl.comment:
System control is the management and regulation of various parameters within the electrical grid to ensure its stable and reliable operation. The primary goal of system control is to maintain the balance between electricity generation and consumption, while also managing factors such as voltage, frequency, and power quality. This involves the use of control devices, automation, and monitoring systems to respond to changes in the grid and maintain its overall stability.
This serves as Integrated AC and DC control system (IEC 60633) which governs the integrated operation of AC and DC systems of a power system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#SystemOperationCoo.comment: A role that coordinates relevant information and impact in regards to operating the power system.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#TCSCController.comment: TCSC controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the performance of the TCSC.

https://cim.ucaiug.io/ns#TapChanger.comment: Mechanism for changing transformer winding tap positions.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#TapChangerControll.comment: Tap changer controller is an equipment controller that controls a tap changer, e.g. how the voltage at the end of a line varies with the load level and compensation of the voltage drop by tap adjustment.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ThyristorControlle.label: ThyristorControlledSeriesCompensator
https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#ThyristorControlle.comment: Thyristor-controlled series capacitors (TCSC) is a type of flexible AC transmission system regulating equipment that is configured with controlled reactors in parallel with sections of a capacitor bank. This combination allows smooth control of the fundamental frequency capacitive reactance over a wide range. The thyristor valve contains a string of series connected high power thyristors. TCSC can control power flows in order to achieve eliminating of line overloads, reducing loop flows and minimising system losses.

https://cim4.eu/ns/nc#TieCorridor.comment: A collection of one or more tie-lines or direct current poles that connect two different control areas.
